_source: Mined 23 Oct 2026 from 16 real xHire interviews (calls >=10 min where the candidate spoke 700+ words), plus the two the owner remembers (prioritise, sell to an executive who won't budge). Groups = left rail (vertical). Variations = horizontal tabs inside a group: the different ways interviewers phrase the same question.

groups.name: Tell me about yourself
variations: Tell me about yourself.
Give us a little introduction of yourself.
Walk me through your background and what you want to highlight.
Tell me about the reporting work you did at your current company.
Can you give me a brief overview of yourself, titles and things you've done?

groups.name: Why are you looking / why this role
variations: Why are you looking to leave your current role?
Why are you interested in this role?
What has you looking for a new position now?
What are you looking for in your next role?
What got you interested in our company?
You're already a subject matter expert where you are. Why move?

groups.name: What do you know about us
variations: What do you know about our company?
What have you learned about us so far?
What can you say about our culture?

groups.name: Prioritising
variations: How do you prioritise?
How do you handle conflicting priorities?
You have two or three projects coming at once. How do you handle it?
How do you prioritise across a global team and multiple regions?
How do you handle tight deadlines and pressure?

groups.name: Selling to an executive who won't budge
variations: How do you convince an executive who won't budge?
How did you make them care?
What happens if they want you to go the wrong direction?
Leadership disagrees with what your data shows. What do you do?
How do you get buy-in when stakeholders aren't sold on your idea?
Tell me about a time you influenced a decision without authority.

groups.name: Stakeholders & requirements
variations: A leader asked for one report but actually needed something different. What did you do?
What's your process when a new requirement comes in?
How do you handle a stakeholder who keeps changing requirements?
Have you renegotiated a timeline with someone more senior?
Tell me about a time you had to say no to a stakeholder.
How do you get people to actually adopt something new you built?

groups.name: Checking the numbers are right
variations: How do you validate a report before it goes to leadership?
How did you turn questionable data into clean data you trusted?
The business says these numbers are wrong. How do you look into it?
Tell me about a time you missed an error before it went out.
How do you document your data cleaning?

groups.name: Dashboards you built
variations: What dashboards have you built?
What visuals and functionality does your dashboard have?
Walk me through one you built end to end and how it solved the problem.
How were the executives using them?
What did the team do with that data?

groups.name: Power BI & data models
variations: How would you troubleshoot a measure that's right at row level but wrong in the total?
Describe the most difficult DAX calculation you've written.
How many models, fact tables and dimensions did you build to support those reports?
How do users access the reports? Workspace or apps? How do you manage who sees what (RLS)?
How do you develop and deploy a report?
How do you optimize a slow Power BI report?
Which Microsoft Fabric components have you implemented?
Rate your Power BI skills from 0 to 10.

groups.name: SQL
variations: What's the difference between an inner join and a left join?
What is a window function and when would you use one?
Have you optimized a query that wasn't performing well? How?
Do you use views or materialized views? When?
How do you find and handle duplicates?
Do you test queries in a separate environment?

groups.name: Pipelines & warehouse
variations: Walk me through a pipeline from raw source data to metrics.
What do you call each layer, and what belongs in each?
Where should transformation logic live: warehouse or BI layer?
How would you pull data from an API into a database or Google Sheet?
Someone does a process by hand. How would you automate it?

groups.name: AI & tools
variations: How is AI changing your work? Have you built anything with it?
What AI tools do you use to support your work?
What are most people doing wrong when using AI to get work done?
What tools, platforms and databases have you used?
How many years of Tableau do you have?
How have you used Python in your current role?

groups.name: Tell me about a time
variations: Tell me about a time you collaborated really well with others. What did you do?
Tell me about a time you worked with a difficult person.
Your work was challenged as incomplete. How did you respond?
Tell me about a time you took initiative.
Tell me about a time documentation helped you.
Tell me about your most complex project or biggest technical challenge.

groups.name: Leadership
variations: What's your leadership style?
Is a team of five the largest you've led?
You've led a team. Are you OK being an individual contributor?
Tell me about a time you stepped into a leadership role.

groups.name: Strengths, weaknesses, why you
variations: What are your strengths?
What's your weakness? A skill you're still developing?
What constructive feedback have you received and how did you act on it?
What sets you apart from other candidates?
Why should we hire you?

groups.name: Salary
variations: What are your salary expectations?
Is that still the range you're looking for?
Where do you sit on that range realistically?
What would you need in a package to consider a change?

groups.name: Logistics
variations: How soon can you start?
Do you have offers elsewhere? What's your timeline?
Are you subject to a non-compete?
This is remote with some travel. Does that work?
Are you authorized to work in the US?

groups.name: Questions for them
variations: What questions do you have for me?
What does success look like in the first 90 days?
What's the biggest problem the team is facing today?
What are the current initiatives?
